finding:
Literal scope. Fix the isotype, the norm half twist and I=[−a,a], a>0. The p. 14 paragraph calls finite sums of the bare tensors |·|_F^(ρ−1/2)(log|·|_F)^m ⊗ ψ_{ρ,m} smooth functions, in input-then-output tensor order; it claims convergence in L²(ν⊗ν∨), with x the output and y the input in the ensuing Haar integral. Here ν=wμ, ν∨=w⁻¹μ and w(g)=max(|g|_F^(−2a),|g|_F^(2a))(1+|log|g|_F|²)^(s/2), exactly the weights in (1.2.1.1). It identifies the integral with A_spec,I(φ) on the completed quotient. In what follows μ̄ means this same Haar measure on the class group, denoted μ in the display. At s=0 the inherited labels are all orders below the multiplicity of interior zeros, starting at m=0, in increasing absolute ordinate; the tests φ are compact smooth with supp φ over norm >1+ε. The bare factors, quotient vectors and ordering do not depend on φ; neither does any fixed lift of those vectors. The preceding display instead uses A(φ)' applied to each jet. Calling the bare limit k_spec,I,φ does not insert this transpose, and a quotient class by itself cannot be used as a function of x or y. No fixed lift and subsequent quotient can cure test-independence. Even changing valid representatives with φ cannot alter the finite actions after applying Q on the output; if the kernels converge as claimed, the projected actions also converge by the Hilbert–Schmidt estimate below. This note dispositions only the p. 14 kernel passage, not the preceding expansion, the opening of p. 15, or item (3).

Coefficient check. Write h=ρ−1/2 and c_h(g)=χ(g)|g|_F^h in the source Mellin convention. The strip variable is shifted once on the already half-twisted ambient profiles; (10.2.2.4) and (10.4.3.39) include χ even though the short p. 14 paragraph does not. For the inverse-left translation convention of p. 14 the input profile transforms by χ(k)⁻¹ under evaluation at ky on the norm-one group; the linear Haar density transforms by χ(k). Use the bilinear pairing ∫f v dμ̄, not ∫conj(f) v dμ̄. If instead a Riesz vector r is used with inner product linear in f, its Haar density is v=w·conj(r). For an interior jet L_{ρ,m}(f)=∫ f(g)c_h(g)(log|g|_F)^m dμ̄(g), change x=gy in L_{ρ,m}(A(φ)f). On compact smooth inputs this gives the transpose Haar density v_{ρ,m,φ}(y)=∫φ(g)c_h(gy)(log|gy|_F)^m dμ̄(g). Equivalently it is the sum over 0≤j≤m of binom(m,j) times ∫φ(g)c_h(g)(log|g|_F)^(m−j)dμ̄(g) times c_h(y)(log|y|_F)^j. Interior densities c_h(y)(log|y|_F)^j belong to the reciprocal-weight L² by strict exponential decay on both tails. By compact-support density in weighted L² and boundedness of compact convolution (the weight ratio under translations on a compact set of log norms is uniformly bounded), the computation holds on the Hilbert space. This yields a pulled-back quotient functional only once the bare jet annihilates the actual closed theta subspace and convolution preserves it. At m=0 the multiplier is M(φ)(c_h), with neither conjugation nor a minus sign in h.

Genuine degree-zero test, in ordinary mathematics. Take F=ℚ, trivial norm-one isotype, a=1/2, and a nontrivial zeta zero ρ with 0<Re ρ<1 (classical existence; no simplicity or location on the critical line is needed). The gamma factor is finite and nonzero there, so this is a retained zero for the completed L-function, h strictly interior, and m=0 is retained. Write t=|g|_ℚ, u=log t. Each class has a positive real representative with all finite components units, uniquely after clearing finite valuations by a positive rational and fixing the real sign. On radial profiles Haar is C du, C>0. Here is the bridge for the whole radial theta range, not just assumption of a descended jet. Average adelic inputs over finite units and real sign; this preserves both zero moments and leaves the trivial-isotype theta profile unchanged. The invariant finite factors are finite linear combinations of product ball indicators 1_{rẐ}, r∈ℚ_{>0}: on their finite active places a unit-invariant locally constant compact profile is constant on valuation strata and on a small ball at zero, and each stratum is a difference of balls. For a factor g_∞⊗1_{rẐ}, the nonzero rational summation set is (rℤ)∖{0}; replace it by g_∞(r·)⊗1_Ẑ. At zero the real value is unchanged, and the real integral is scaled by r⁻¹, the volume of the replaced ball (normalize vol Ẑ=1). Thus after combining terms the full radial range consists of profiles t^(1/2)Σ_{n≠0}b(nt), with b even Schwartz, b(0)=0 and ∫b=0. The sum is rapidly decreasing as t→∞ by Schwartz decay, and as t↓0 by Poisson summation and the two zero moments. Its untwisted Mellin transform at z for Re z>1 is 2ζ(z)∫₀^∞b(t)t^z dt/t by absolute unfolding; the transform of the theta sum is entire and the b integral holomorphic for Re z>0. Analytic continuation gives vanishing at ρ, also to the full zero order. This is exactly the evaluation against t^h on the once-twisted profile (up to the Haar constant). Cauchy–Schwarz against w⁻¹ therefore extends L_{ρ,0} to a functional ℓ on the quotient by the full closed half-twisted radial theta range. If U is an original representative of the printed biorthogonal at (ρ,0), the original pairing 1 passes to ℓ(QU)=1: the twist changes the exponent by −1/2 and subtracting an element of the closed range does not change the pairing. The same reasoning preserves its Kronecker row on the other original vectors. No assertion about totality is used.

For test variation one need not assume existence of those original biorthogonals. Set φ₁(g)=β(u)e^(−hu) with nonnegative nonzero β∈C_c^∞ supported in an interval strictly above log(1+ε), and λ=C∫β(u)du>0. This is a compact smooth class test, including the compact unit factor. The compact smooth ambient input f=φ₁/λ has ℓ(Qf)=1. Convolution descends in this example: log translations by v are bounded by the ratio w(u+v)/w(u)≤e^|v| and strongly continuous by density; t→t/e^v on a half-twisted theta profile replaces b by e^(−v/2)b(e^(−v)·), preserving both moments. The closed range is invariant under the compact log convolution integral. By the transpose computation, ℓ(A_spec,I(φ₁) Qf)=λ, while ℓ(A_spec,I(0) Qf)=0. The zero test has empty support and satisfies the same support condition; φ₁ and 2φ₁ also give different values without using zero. In particular the same nonzero pairing λ is obtained on the retained source vector when using its original normalization. Independently, when using fixed lifts and the source biorthogonality, the bare finite operators are the coordinate maps: on applying Q and then ℓ to the lifted action on that vector the coefficient is 1 for every cutoff retaining its slot, whereas all the regularized operators for φ=0 are zero. These are finite identities; if the bare kernels converged in the claimed weighted L², continuity of the integral operator map below would preserve that fixed pairing. More generally the fixed bare sequence, if convergent, has only one limit, which cannot realize the two tested operators, even after passing back to the quotient. This does not infer divergence, use cancellation of an unbounded infinite series, or disprove a regularized expansion.

Conditional kernel repair. Let H_χ be the ambient weighted isotype in H=L²(C_F,ν); let E=H_χ/N for the closed half-twisted theta isotype N, Q the quotient, S the isometric section to N⊥ in H_χ, and P=SQ. For the claimed regularized quotient partial sum B_T use S B_T Q, extended by zero on other isotypes when represented on H. Its kernel in output-input order is K_T(x,y)=Σ(Sψ_{ρ,m})(x) v_{ρ,m,φ}(y), where v_{ρ,m,φ} is the Haar density of (ℓ_{ρ,m}∘A_spec,I(φ))∘Q (with the isotype projection on the input if working on H). An arbitrary representative for an output vector need not give that operator. If k_ν is the Hilbert–Schmidt kernel relative to ν in the input, K=w(y)k_ν gives the same action relative to μ̄, and ||K||_{L²(ν⊗ν∨)}=||k_ν||_{L²(ν⊗ν)}. This is the Hilbert–Schmidt correspondence of (C.3.6.5)–(C.3.6.9) with variables transposed from the input-first convention. On a rank one u(x)v(y) its squared norm is ||u||²_{L²(ν)} ||v||²_{L²(ν∨)}. Under the orthogonal decomposition the nonzero singular values of S(B_T−B_U)Q are precisely those of B_T−B_U. Thus ||K_T−K_U||_{L²(ν⊗ν∨)}=||B_T−B_U||₂≤||B_T−B_U||₁. If B_T converges to A_spec,I(φ) in trace norm, the repaired limit represents S A_spec,I(φ) Q by Haar integration for almost every output x for each input; Cauchy–Schwarz applies to almost every row. The kernel class is unique in weighted L² for this ambient operator, and the quotient action is recovered by Q. Neither the integral nor the output classes supply pointwise or smooth representatives, in particular no diagonal values.

Theorem 10.4.3.5(2) states projective tensor convergence at s>1 and already prints the transpose and lifts in (10.4.3.42)–(10.4.3.43); it does not give the bare formula or the introductory s=0 limit. Its §10.4.3.2 lead-in refers to the estimates of Theorem 10.4.2.8. The map of (10.4.3.44) applied to the lifted tensors acts as S B_T Q; as .godel/obligations/trace-spectral.md records, Q A=A_spec,I Q gives S A_spec,I Q=P A, not A P unless (1−P)A P=0 on this isotype. (10.4.3.45) prints A P and its preceding sentence even cites the quotient tensor number (10.4.3.42). The printed introductory rule uses a max and (10.2.2.5) uses a min with a different cutoff; the latter still needs a strict endpoint check when (s−1)/2 is integral.
